label: def:quantum-observable-universe
title: Quantum Observable Universe
html:
Definition. Quantum Observable Universe

A quantum universe (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) over R is a quantum observable universe if the forgetful functor \tau is faithful and five conditions hold:

  1. (Rigidity) Every object V \in \mathbf{C} has a dual V^{\vee}, with evaluation \mathrm{ev}_V \colon V \otimes V^{\vee} \to \mathbf{1} and coevaluation \mathrm{coev}_V \colon \mathbf{1} \to V^{\vee} \otimes V satisfying the snake identities.
  2. (Non-degenerate integration) The Frobenius form \int_A \colon A \to \mathbf{1} induces an isomorphism A \xrightarrow{\sim} A^{\vee} via the pairing (a, b) \mapsto \int_A ab.
  3. (Observability) There are no hidden global symmetries: \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0.
  4. (Measurability) The categorical Chern classes of the adjoint object vanish: c_1(\mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 and c_2(\mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0.
  5. (Categorical volume constraint) The exterior square of the fundamental object V is a quotient \pi \colon V \otimes V \twoheadrightarrow \Lambda^2 V, and there is an isomorphism \epsilon \colon \Lambda^2 V \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \mathbf{1} preserved by all tensor automorphisms:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:categorical-volume-constraint}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  \Lambda^2 V \ar[r, "\Lambda^2 g_V"]
              \ar[d, "\epsilon"', two heads]
  & \Lambda^2 V \ar[d, "\epsilon", two heads]
  \\
  \mathbf{1} \ar[r, "g_{\mathbf{1}} = \mathrm{id}"']
  & \mathbf{1}
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}

A quantum universe is thus braided; a quantum observable universe is braided and rigid.

On "non-degenerate epimorphism" in condition 5. Earlier statements of this definition wrote \epsilon as a non-degenerate epimorphism. That phrase admits two readings of unequal strength, and only the stronger one does the work the framework asks of condition 5:

reading of \epsilon dimension statement forces
epimorphism onto \mathbf{1} \binom{N}{2} \neq 0 N \geq 2 — admits the colour fibre N = 3
isomorphism \Lambda^2 V \cong \mathbf{1} \binom{N}{2} = 1 \mathbf{N = 2}

Both rows are proved in lean/QOU/BraidsAndKnots/VolumeConstraintForcesFibreTwo.lean (exteriorSquareDim_ne_zero_iff, exteriorSquareDim_eq_one_iff). The isomorphism is the intended reading: \det(g) is the scalar by which g acts on the top exterior power \Lambda^N V, so a constraint imposed on \Lambda^2 V is a determinant constraint exactly when 2 = N. Under the weak reading \epsilon constrains only the second elementary symmetric function of the eigenvalues, and the step to \det(g_V) = 1 — the whole point of condition 5 — does not go through. Non-degeneracy is precisely what upgrades the epimorphism to an isomorphism, so the diagram's \twoheadrightarrow remains correct, just no longer the strongest thing true of \epsilon.
